issues.label: Standard of review for PCR denial
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standard—abuse of discretion or de novo—to reviewing the denial.

issues.label: Timeliness/jurisdiction of PCR petition
issues.why: Whether the petition was filed within statutory deadlines affects the trial court's jurisdiction to consider it.

issues.label: Effect of miscited R.C. 2953.21(C)
issues.why: The petition cited a death-penalty provision, raising whether the correct statutory basis governs and whether miscitation is fatal.

issues.label: Entitlement to evidentiary hearing
issues.why: The court must determine if the petition and evidence outside the record warranted a hearing under R.C. 2953.21.

issues.label: Whether petition contained sufficient operative facts
issues.why: A hearing is required only if petitioner presents evidence demonstrating substantive grounds for relief.

issues.label: Res judicata bar to IAC claim
issues.why: Claims that could have been raised on direct appeal may be barred unless supported by evidence outside the record.

issues.label: Mootness based on Johnson I
issues.why: Whether the appellate affirmance actually renders the IAC claim moot must be assessed.

issues.label: New evidence outside trial record
issues.why: Evidence dehors the record may defeat res judicata and mootness, requiring the court to consider it.

issues.label: Ineffective assistance of counsel merits
issues.why: The Strickland deficient-performance and prejudice standard governs the underlying claim.

issues.label: Adequacy of findings of fact/conclusions
issues.why: R.C. 2953.21(H) and Penland require sufficient findings and conclusions to permit review.

issues.label: Remedy if findings inadequate
issues.why: The court must decide whether to remand for adequate findings or resolve the matter itself.

issues.label: Application to no-contest plea case
issues.why: Case 22CRC-I0207 involved a no-contest plea, and PCR standards must be applied to that distinct conviction.

issues.label: Consolidation of two separate cases
issues.why: The petition spans two case numbers with different pleas and sentences, requiring case-specific analysis.

issues.label: Forfeiture specification implications
issues.why: The handgun forfeiture may raise separate procedural or substantive considerations.

issues.label: Whether error was harmless
issues.why: Even if the trial court erred, the court must assess prejudice to petitioner.
